solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Recap, standard, covering rotating machine

indicators.note: the two words cover the answer, holding it across their join

explanation.surface: An instruction to summarise and standardise, with a machine tacked on as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals the answer sits inside 'Recap, standard', ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship, turned to wind in cable or rope.

clue.text: Put together polemic for change

indicators.note: for change says the word is to be changed, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: Assembling a campaigning tract that demands reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for change' rearranges POLEMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to collect material and assemble it into a whole.

clue.text: Privileged Roman pair I can't reform

indicators.note: to reform is to make over in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An entitled Roman admits he cannot change a couple of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges PAIRICANT; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricians were the hereditary aristocratic class of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Herb that's a surprise to see brought up in article

indicators.note: in places the reversed exclamation inside the article

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: brought up suits a down entry: the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: 'my!' is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A herb that startles someone when it appears in a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a news piece; it is the grammatical one. 'brought up' suits a down light, where reversed letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a fragrant herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Important person drops by casualty in US, easy decision

parts.note: a nob is a person of high social standing
rain falls as drops
ER, the emergency room, is the American name for a hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: A VIP calls into a US emergency room, an obvious choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops by' reads as visiting; 'drops' is rain and 'by' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is a choice so obvious that it needs no thought.

clue.text: Drama to upset Ring performer?

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over and throw it into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatrical row threatens to disrupt a performance of Wagner's Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges DRAMATO. 'Ring' suggests opera or boxing; the question mark warns it is the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador performs before crowds in the bullring, the arena where bullfights are staged.

clue.text: Join Republicans in 31 days

indicators.note: in puts the Republicans inside the month

parts.note: May is a month of 31 days
R is short for Republican, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: An invitation to join the Republican party within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: '31 days' could be several months; only MAY fits the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry is to join two people, or to unite two things.

clue.text: Managed some inmates initially in shelter not intended to last

indicators.note: in places the run of letters inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A refuge run for a few inmates at first was only ever temporary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives SI from 'some inmates'; RAN plus SI goes 'in' TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means passing or short-lived, lasting only briefly.

clue.text: This leads to advantage in court

definitions.text: This leads to advantage in court

parts.words: This leads to advantage in court
parts.note: in tennis, the tied score of forty-all is followed by 'advantage' to whoever wins the next point

explanation.surface: Sounds like a legal tactic that gains the upper hand at trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advantage' and 'court' suggest a lawsuit; the court is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, forty-all is called by this name, and the next point won gives advantage.

clue.text: Have another go at harvest work

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
to ply is to work at, as in ply a trade

explanation.surface: A farmer tries once more at bringing in the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: To reapply is to apply again, making a fresh attempt or application.

clue.text: Friendly parent still around

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, a parent

indicators.note: around tells us the word for still is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: still in the sense 'yet', as in 'yet to come'

explanation.surface: A mother or father who remains sociable and is still on the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey is informal British for sociable and familiar, like a mate or pal.

clue.text: Pub artist with something to chew, a fish

parts.note: a bar is a pub
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
cud is the food cattle chew over again

explanation.surface: A painter in a pub, munching on something, orders a fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The barracuda is a predatory sea fish with long sharp teeth.

clue.text: The very thing, popular — period railway journey plan

parts.note: 'it' is the very thing, as in 'that's it!'
in means fashionable or popular
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fashionable period-style railway trip is exactly what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is the planned route and schedule for a trip.

clue.text: Soak, high

definitions.meaning: ... means high, as in a ... price or slope

explanation.surface: Two bare words suggesting a drenched and towering scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeping tea means soaking it; a steep cliff or price is a high one.

clue.text: Leave catching start of show, live

indicators.note: the word for leave catches, or holds inside it, the next letter

parts.note: to exit is to leave

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Walking out after catching the opening of a live show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes S from 'show'; 'catching' puts it inside EXIT. 'live' looks like an adjective (a live show) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to have being, to be alive.

clue.text: Celebrating uniform speed in test

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Delight after a uniform pace is achieved during a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphal describes something marking a victory, as in a triumphal arch or procession.

clue.text: Top, recently acquired, in a state!

parts.note: new describes something just obtained
a jersey is a knitted top

explanation.surface: Someone is all worked up about a top they have just bought.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces in the other order. 'in a state' reads as being agitated, but 'a state' is the US one.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Lively girls went for sport

indicators.note: lively means full of movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Energetic girls headed off to play a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lively' rearranges GIRLSWENT; 'for' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrestling is a combat sport of grappling and throwing an opponent.

clue.text: Extremely silly to replace leader of show group

indicators.note: the outer letters take the place of the first letter of the word for show

parts.note: to indicate is to show

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the outer letters, of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Something very daft takes over the top billing of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives SY from 'silly'; it replaces the I that leads INDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group of people or firms joined for a shared venture.

clue.text: Building employee unfortunately egocentric, forgetting time

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put into disorder
forgetting means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A porter at an apartment block turns out to be self-absorbed and forgetful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' removes T from EGOCENTRIC; 'unfortunately' shuffles the remaining EGOCENRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A concierge is a caretaker or doorkeeper employed by a block of flats or hotel.

clue.text: Check as sibling briefly shows car part

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, its ending dropped

parts.note: a sister is a sibling

explanation.surface: A brother or sister quickly inspects a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SISTER to SIS; 'shows' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The chassis is the base frame of a car on which the body is mounted.

clue.text: Swimmer heading away from unpleasant smell

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, goes away from the word for unpleasant smell

parts.note: a stench is a nasty smell

explanation.surface: A swimmer moving away from a nasty odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading away from' removes S from STENCH. 'Swimmer' hints at a person; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Deceived about no good own goal, miserable

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for deceived surrounds the next piece

parts.note: to be had is to be deceived or tricked
OG is the abbreviation for an own goal in football

explanation.surface: A footballer tricked into a useless own goal feels wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: OG for own goal is a football scoring abbreviation; 'about' wraps the first word around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and dejected, like a guilty dog.

clue.text: "All About Me" — oddly a collector's item

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters: first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A self-titled memoir or record is touted as a collectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of ALLABOUTME.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectors keep stamps, photos or cards in an album, a book made for the purpose.

clue.text: Support couple

definitions.meaning: a ... is a pair, as in a ... of pheasants

explanation.surface: Two words suggesting a pair helping each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace props up a structure, and a brace of game birds is two of them.

clue.text: Unit's total ban I revised

indicators.note: revised means altered and reworked, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier says his unit's complete prohibition has been amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges TOTALBANI; the 's is 'is', joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a military unit of several companies.

clue.text: Set timer wife's seen as second-rate

indicators.note: seen as says one letter now appears as another, a swap

parts.note: a watch is a timer
W is the abbreviation for wife; the 's is 'is'
B is second-rate, as in a B grade

explanation.surface: A husband judges the clock his wife set to be second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like the verb; it is the noun meaning a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a set of things made or dealt with together.

clue.text: Crime clergyman quietly ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the quiet letter is left out

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman
P is piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A vicar's misdeed passed over without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Get at ship's exotic food

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are made unfamiliar by rearranging them

parts.note: ship is the fodder; the 's is 'is', joining it to the indicator

explanation.surface: An invitation to try the unusual meals served aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges GETATSHIP; 'ship's' reads as possessive but is 'ship is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is long thin pasta, an Italian staple food.

clue.text: Small charge for turf

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a ward is a person in someone's care, their charge

explanation.surface: A minor fee for laying grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests a fee but here means someone in your care.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass, that is, turf.

clue.text: Cunning bargain, that (not half)!

parts.note: a steal is something bought very cheaply, a bargain

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, here its first two letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a deal is a real bargain, 'not half!' meaning 'and how!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves TH from 'that'. 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secret, crafty action, the sort of cunning that avoids notice.

clue.text: Plant using drinks, English

parts.note: gins are drinks

explanation.surface: An English gardener uses alcohol to grow something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginseng is an Asian herb whose root is prized as a tonic.
